vehicle.mass_note: Measured with setup wheel adapters, 75kg driver, 35kg fuel. Adapters cancel in ratios.

corner_weights.note: RR calculated: total - FL - FR - RL. Measured on setup patch including adapters.

vehicle.yaw_inertia_note: Estimated from Iz = m*a*b bicycle model approximation. Error ~10-20%. Replace with homologation value when available.
vehicle.steering_ratio_note: Read from steering ratio lookup table at centre wheel travel and zero steering stroke. Treated as constant at Level 1.
vehicle.cog_note: Derived from static weight distribution. a = L * rear_fraction, b = L * front_fraction.

stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (modules/yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal). These are the values the chair pipeline actually runs (its dataclass defaults / default invocation) -- changing any of the six re-triggers classification-threshold re-derivation (WP5b(e) pattern), since thresholds are tuned to this estimator's output distribution.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback cornering stiffness references. Derived from axle normal load × C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad⁻¹ (Milliken & Milliken, RCVD, GT3 slick). Front: (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268. Rear: (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Used as C_linear_ref when OLS cannot resolve the linear stiffness from data (insufficient alpha excitation on rear axle). Accuracy Level 1.

classification._comment: Corner-verdict thresholds for ui/views/outing_form.py's _classify_corner. accuracy_levels._comment: Single source of truth for per-quantity accuracy (1=config default, 2=session measurement, 3=logged sensor, 4=lookup table; upgrade each node independently, CLAUDE.md/thesis_notes.md). Each node: level (current STATIC/default tier, what a run with no session data resolves to), source (what currently provides the value), capped_by (why it isn't higher: 'chained-constant: <name>' when a Level-1 config constant sits in the node's own derivation chain, 'provenance-assumption: <name>' when no such constant exists but a documented, unverifiable assumption about the channel's own measurement caps it anyway, or null when neither mechanism applies). Consolidated 2026-07-26 -- see thesis_notes.md for the yaw_rate=3 vs steering_angle=1 resolution evidence. WP-C (2026-07-26) adds per-session dynamic resolution on top of this static registry, in modules/accuracy_resolution.py: leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, and in future WPs steering_ratio/speed/sideslip_angle) carry a real ordered source list there and resolve independently per outing; derived nodes have no source list of their own and instead cascade from the nodes named in capped_by -- either a PURE cascade (resolved level = input's resolved level exactly, e.g. cog_position from corner_weights) or a METHOD-CEILINGED cascade bounded by an explicit method_ceiling field below (the derivation is itself an approximation whose error a better-measured input cannot shrink, e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b formula). Every node not dynamically wired yet stays single-source at its level below regardless of any global cap, until its own future WP gives it a second source.

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); dynamically resolves to Level 4 (car_data.json steering_ratio_table, manufacturer digitised) when that local-only file is present and the cap allows it -- modules/accuracy_resolution.py. Parameterization, not a chair-comparison deviation: the constant was never a chair scientific position, it is this car's own mechanical steering geometry.

speed.capped_by: provenance-assumption: opaque ECU wheel-speed calibration (thesis_notes.md limitations register item 10)

yaw_rate.source: sclu_yaw_rate logged channel, exact rpm-to-radps unit conversion

steering_angle.source: log_asteer logged channel, converted via steering_ratio (pure cascade -- resolves to steering_ratio's own resolved level, WP-B)

lateral_acc.source: log_acc_y logged channel, exact g-to-mps2 unit conversion

wheelbase_m.note: Fixed chassis dimension, known to design tolerance; not expected to move enough to justify a dedicated remeasurement -- kept at Level 1 by convention, not as a live upgrade target.
